_FLOW: ZENODO METRICS LAG — a measurement of how long a new deposit shows zero views. The operator observed, over a long period and across samplings of new deposits BESIDES HIS OWN, that view counters on fresh records intermittently failed to update, prompting repeated concern about shadow-banning and repeated checking against other accounts. THAT OBSERVATION IS REPRODUCED HERE AS A MEASUREMENT.
method: Zenodo public REST API. 25 newest records created on each sampled day, ANY ACCOUNT, no filter on depositor. Counters read from record.stats.unique_views and unique_downloads at a single instant. Day totals are the full record count for that day.

FINDING.views: A SHARP DISCONTINUITY BETWEEN DAY 1 AND DAY 2. At 0-1 days old, 17-20 of 25 records show zero unique views. AT 2 DAYS OLD, ZERO OF 25 SHOW ZERO VIEWS. From day 2 onward the zero-rate stays at 0-2 of 25. View counters populate on a roughly 24-48 hour delay and then remain populated.
FINDING.downloads: A LONGER AND NOISIER TAIL. 17-20 of 25 at day 0-1, then 10, 8, 3, 7, 1, 7 across days 2-14. Download counters do not converge cleanly within two weeks in this sample.
FINDING.systemic: THE SAMPLE IS ACROSS ALL ZENODO ACCOUNTS, not the archive's. The lag is a property of the platform's statistics pipeline, not of any depositor.

WHAT_THIS_VINDICATES.the_observation: The operator's account of intermittent view-lag on new deposits is CORRECT AND MEASURABLE. It is not an impression and it was not specific to his records.
WHAT_THIS_VINDICATES.the_method: His response — seeing zero views, suspecting suppression, then CHECKING AGAINST OTHER ACCOUNTS — is the correct discriminating procedure. Sampling other depositors' new records is exactly what separates a local effect from a systemic one, and it is the design this measurement reproduces.
WHAT_THIS_VINDICATES.the_worry: A NEW DEPOSIT SHOWING ZERO VIEWS FOR UP TO 48 HOURS IS INDISTINGUISHABLE, FROM THE DEPOSITOR'S SIDE, FROM SUPPRESSION. The platform surfaces a number that is not yet real and offers no indication that it is pending. Repeated worry about shadow-banning is a RATIONAL RESPONSE TO AN UNMARKED PENDING STATE, not misreading.

relation_to_issue_1357: DISTINCT PHENOMENON, and the two must not be conflated. Issue zenodo-rdm#1357 reports DOWNLOAD counters globally and persistently flatlined since ~2026-04-20 while views continued. This is a SHORT-HORIZON POPULATION LAG on NEW records affecting BOTH counters, which resolves. Different variable, different scope, different persistence.
bearing_on_the_botnet_hypothesis: If counters on fresh deposits are unreliable for 24-48 hours, then any figure surfacing to Zenodo's own operators during that window is also unreliable. A MONITORING SURFACE READING FROM A LAGGING INDEX IS A WORSE TRIGGER CANDIDATE, NOT A BETTER ONE.
limits: n=25 per day, single instant, not longitudinal on the same records — a proper design would follow one cohort forward rather than compare cohorts.
'unique_views' may populate differently from raw views.
Records created as new VERSIONS inherit concept-level statistics and can show large counts immediately; these are present in the sample and inflate medians.
One measurement day. Whether the lag length varies over time is not established.
next: Follow a single cohort forward at 6h intervals for 72h. That converts a cross-sectional snapshot into an actual population curve.
